findings.title: A failed `git diff` in `shelve` writes an empty patch, then the work is restored away
quotes: written with `write_bytes` before anything is applied or restored (as today)
findings.fix: take `code, diff, err = records.git(..., raw=True)` and, if `code != 0`, raise or return before writing the patch or restoring anything. Add a test where `git diff` fails and the tree stays untouched.

sources.situation: `shelve` calls `records.git(root, "diff", "HEAD", "--binary", "--", *paths, raw=True)[1]` and never looks at the exit code, which `raw` returns as element 0. If `git diff` fails (index lock held by a concurrent git process, a failed `add -N`, a corrupt object), stdout is `b""`. `path.write_bytes(b"")` then "succeeds". The loop below it runs `git checkout -q HEAD -- p` on every kept path. The task's work is gone and the only record is an empty patch, so the comment "the work is never only in the tree" no longer holds. `land` has the same swallowed code. There the empty patch happens to make `git apply` fail, but the cause is lost.

`git diff HEAD` exits non-zero, for example on an unreadable path or a pathspec error after `add -N`. `[1]` throws away the exit code. An empty or partial `T-n.patch` is written, and then every path is checked out to HEAD or unlinked. The task's uncommitted work then exists neither in the tree nor in the patch, and can't be recovered. `land` is protected because `git apply` fails on a bad patch and `restore` runs; `shelve` has no such guard. No test covers a failing diff in `shelve`.

findings.reason: `shelve` in `src/nio/implement.py` (line 454) takes `records.git(..., raw=True)[1]` and drops the exit code that `raw` returns. Line 457 then writes the possibly empty patch, and the loop at lines 458-463 checks out or unlinks every path. Nothing in CT-5 or the code guards against a failed `git diff`.

findings.title: Every edit after any rejected round re-runs all voting lenses, with no bound on spend
quotes: applies at the spec, plan and tasks gates (`gate in GATES`) once any round was recorded `rejected`
findings.fix: key the rule on the last recorded round, or on the last outcome being `rejected` with every finding disposed. Say which in CT-7.

sources.situation: the new condition is `any(o == "rejected" for _, o in led["recorded"])`, so one old rejection counts forever. Every later edit that changes an ID or section, even a one-word rewording, makes `step` start a model run of every lens that ever voted. This holds when the last outcome is `human` or `rerun`, and when the findings are all disposed. Repeated small edits cost juror calls and the human's attention each time. FR-10's own scenario is narrower: a rejected round whose only finding was accepted as risk.

findings.title: The moved-artefact guard is bypassed by the actor it is meant to stop
quotes: when `step.json` is absent (a run driven by hand with `nio jury collect`)
findings.fix: record the version in the ledger when the packs are written, not in a file the juror can reach. Treat a missing or versionless `step.json` in a `step`-driven run as refused.

sources.situation: AC-13's threat is a lens juror that edits the spec it judges. That juror has file write access to the run folder. It can delete `jury/packs/step.json`, which returns without any check, or rewrite its `version`, and then collect the outputs. `moved()` also does `json.loads(sj.read_text())["version"]` with no guard, so a `step.json` from an older run raises a bare `KeyError` instead of the clean refusal. `_reusable` does the same.

findings.title: Patch byte-exactness is only shown with default git config
quotes: each main-tree file equals the worktree's bytes
findings.fix: add a test with `core.autocrlf` and an `eol` attribute set. Either pin the behaviour in the contract or fail loudly when the landed bytes differ.

sources.situation: `test_ac4b_land_keeps_bytes` and `test_misuse_crlf_edit_lands` use a fresh repo with default config. With `core.autocrlf=true` or a `.gitattributes` `text eol=` rule, `git add -A` and `git diff --cached` emit normalised (LF) content for a CRLF working file. Applying that patch to a CRLF main-tree file can fail on context, or write different bytes. The AC passes in tests but may not hold for a CRLF user, who is the very case it names.

findings.title: `land` and `shelve` decode file names as text, so a non-UTF-8 name crashes after the patch is half done
findings.fix: read the name lists with `-z` through `raw`, or decode with `errors="surrogateescape"`. Add a test with such a name.

sources.situation: only the patch is read as bytes. The `--name-only` and `porcelain` calls still use `text=True`, which decodes strictly as UTF-8. A latin-1 file name (Linux allows it; the tests cover latin-1 file contents, not names) raises `UnicodeDecodeError` out of `land` or `shelve`. For `land`, that happens after `add -A` and the patch write, before the apply. For `shelve`, it happens before the patch is saved. The task then neither lands nor is cleanly shelved, and the error is a traceback.

findings.title: Implementation rerun with no lens to re-run opens a run instead of showing the human
quotes: IF a gate's outcome is `rerun` and no lens is named to re-run THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL name no juror
no `run:` line, no run folder, no pack or `step.json`
findings.fix: drop the `gate in GATES` restriction from the guard in `_begin` (so the empty-lens case always returns the show-the-human line before any run is created), or state in CT-6 why the implementation gate is exempt.

sources.situation: at the implementation gate, a round whose outcome is `rerun` but where `changed(...)` names no lens reaches `_begin` with an empty `lenses` and `run` "". The guard `not lenses and (gate in GATES or (run and evidence.path(root, run).exists()))` is false, so `_begin` creates a run folder, writes `step.json` with `"lenses": []`, and prints `run: R-...` followed by `next: nio jury evidence ...`. The spec requires a `next:` line that says to show the human, with no run line and no run folder.

findings.reason: At the implementation gate `GATES` has only spec, plan and tasks (`src/nio/jury.py` line 14). With empty `lenses` and `run` "", the guard at line 1401 is false. `_begin` then reaches `records.new_run` and writes `step.json` with `"lenses": []` (lines 1403-1410). CT-6 says an empty `lenses` gives only the show-the-human line, with no run folder or `step.json`. CT-7 exempts the implementation gate only from the re-run-every-lens rule, not from CT-6.

findings.title: shelve still restores the tree when git diff failed
quotes: `raw` (implies `full`) keeps stdout as bytes, so a patch of it loses nothing (CT-4).
findings.fix: take the exit code from `raw=True` and raise before any checkout or unlink when it is non-zero (the patch stays on disk). Add a test that fakes a failing `diff` and asserts the files are untouched.

findings.title: "restore it" at the implementation gate invites undoing a commit
quotes: restore it, or start a new run (nio jury next without --run)
findings.fix: at the implementation gate, word the message so it says to start a new run, and don't say "restore". Add an assertion in test_ac14 that a step without `--run` then begins a fresh run.

sources.situation: at implementation-E-1 the thing that "changed" is a newly landed task commit. An agent told to "restore it" may `git reset` the epic's new commit to make the run collectable again, which throws away landed work. AC-14 checks only the refusal. No test shows that the "start a new run" path recovers at the implementation gate.
